outcome: rate of exclusive breastfeeding at 6 months
cohort: Neonates born to SARS-CoV-2 infected mothers, categorized into those who experienced mother-infant separation after birth (Cohort A) and those who did not (rooming-in, Cohort B).
finding: Mother-infant separation after birth significantly reduced exclusive breastfeeding rates at 6 months and led to higher infant weight gain compared to rooming-in, while showing no differences in SARS-CoV-2 transmission, acute neonatal infections, or neurodevelopment.
gest_age: Mean 39.0 weeks (Cohort A) vs 38.9 weeks (Cohort B)
